summary.title: The Open Software Assurance Maturity Model
summary.one_liner: SAMM is a vendor-neutral, free OWASP framework for assessing an organization's software security practices and building a measurable, iterative software security program.
takeaways: SAMM is an open, vendor-neutral and freely available framework for software security strategy.
It helps evaluate existing software security practices and build a balanced program in iterations.
It can be applied organization-wide, to a single line of business, or to an individual project.
It is designed to fit small, medium, and large organizations using any development style.
Practices can be assessed against SAMM activities to quantify improvements.
summary.summary: This OWASP project page introduces the Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM), an open framework for organizations to formulate and implement a software security strategy tailored to their risks. It lists goals such as evaluating current practices, building a balanced program in well-defined iterations, demonstrating improvements, and measuring security activities. The page is mostly promotional, with testimonials from Dell, Gotham Digital Science, Fortify Software and others, and it does not detail the model's specific practices or scoring. Its main value is as a pointer to the framework itself.
